about: Open questions for the steps of access that nobody has measured, in the sources checked for each country (November 2026). 'have' restates only what the country's confirmed findings on /social-protection/ measure and do not measure; 'could' and 'scale' are our suggestions, and every scale is illustrative, not a power calculation. convert.js adds these to each country's questions with their steps, and the page links each unmeasured step to its question. Reviewed when a country's findings change: a step that becomes measured loses its question here.

questions.q: When heat arrives, how much of a household's lost earnings and care costs does an allowance or top-up cover, and does it arrive before the hottest days?
questions.have: Implementer reports count households that received cash in Rajshahi and Dhaka. None of the sources checked measures how far the money went, or when it arrived compared with the heat.
questions.could: Follow recipient households through one hot season, recording lost work days, care costs and payment dates against heat-alert dates.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 300 households in two cities over one hot season

questions.q: How many heat-exposed urban households know of an allowance, qualify for it, hold the documents, apply and are enrolled?
questions.have: None of the sources checked measures these steps for the schemes on this page in Bangladesh.
questions.could: A household survey in hot wards that asks the same people about each step, for the same schemes.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 1,000 households in four wards

questions.q: Is what a household receives from rural work, pensions or food rations enough to cover a hot season's lost earnings and care costs?
questions.have: Documents, applications, enrolment, receipt and payment timing are measured for some schemes, such as fund transfer orders for rural work. No source checked measures whether support is adequate in a hot season.
questions.could: Compare the support received with heat-season losses in the same households, in a hot month and a cooler one.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 600 households in three districts

questions.q: How many informal workers exposed to heat know which schemes they could use, and how many of them qualify?
questions.have: Later steps are measured for some schemes; awareness and eligibility are not, in the sources checked.
questions.could: Pair a short awareness survey with an eligibility screen for the same workers, at worksites and markets.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 800 workers in two cities

questions.q: Do cash transfers reach families before or after the hottest weeks, and is the amount enough to cover lost work?
questions.have: Government reports count the families paid each quarter, without payment dates set against heat or amounts set against losses.
questions.could: Link payment dates with heat records and a short household survey on lost work and spending.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 500 families in two provinces over one year

questions.q: Where do informal workers stop between hearing of worker insurance and applying for it?
questions.have: An evaluation in Bandung and Medan measured enrolment: registration help raised it by 3.5 percentage points and full subsidy by 18.6, while information alone had no measured effect. Awareness, documents and applications were not measured as separate steps.
questions.could: Follow the same workers through awareness, documents and application, with and without help to register.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 1,000 workers in two cities

questions.q: Do allowances arrive on time and cover what a hot season costs older people and outdoor-worker households?
questions.have: Awareness of the Social Security Fund, enrolment and receipt are measured in the sources checked; the adequacy and timing of allowances in hot months are not.
questions.could: Record payment dates and heat-season costs for allowance households in the Tarai.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 400 households in four municipalities

questions.q: Among people who qualify for an allowance, how many hold the documents and have applied?
questions.have: In the sources checked, eligibility, documents and applications are not measured as separate steps.
questions.could: A records review with local governments that counts eligible people, documents held and applications made.
questions.scale: Illustrative: six wards in three municipalities

questions.q: Does temporary support cover the income lost when heat cuts work, and how soon does it arrive?
questions.have: Counts of households receiving ComCare support and of workers receiving the Workfare Income Supplement are published; adequacy and timing against heat-related income loss are not, in the sources checked.
questions.could: A survey of support recipients in outdoor work that compares lost earnings in hot months with the support received and when it came.

questions.q: Do migrant workers know which medical and injury protections apply to heat illness, and do they start a claim?
questions.have: None of the sources checked measures awareness, applications or claims started among migrant workers for heat illness.
questions.could: Short surveys at dormitories and worker centres, with partner organisations, followed by records of claims started.

questions.q: For older people and informal workers, which is the first step of access where support stops in a hot season?
questions.have: None of the sources checked measures any step of access for the schemes on this page in Thailand.
questions.could: A household survey that follows the old-age allowance and Section 40 through all eight steps, for the same people.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 1,000 households in three provinces

questions.q: Does crop relief after a declared disaster arrive in time to matter for the next season?
questions.have: None of the sources checked measures when relief reaches farmers compared with the loss.
questions.could: Compare declaration, claim and payment dates for crop relief across districts.
questions.scale: Illustrative: records from ten districts over two seasons
